title: Language-tolerant invocation validators and ergonomic call helpers
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Function/tool-calling across our SDKs needs to be robust when model outputs differ slightly from the declared schema (extra fields, missing optional fields, numeric/string mismatches) and ergonomically easy for app developers to call functions with retries and streaming. Current validators are strict and often cause avoidable failures; retry helpers lack idempotency hooks and streaming resume points across languages. This ticket designs language-level helpers that are tolerant by default, provide deterministic coercion policies, and expose hooks for instrumentation and resume semantics.
proposal: Deliver a small cross-language library surface (Python, TypeScript, Go) that provides: 1) a permissive schema validator with strict-mode opt-in, 2) deterministic coercion rules and sanitizers (string->number, number->string, enum fuzzy match), 3) streaming reassembly helpers to validate partial JSON chunks and resume on reconnect, 4) invocation helpers that wrap call + retry with idempotency tokens and max-attempts backoff policy, and 5) clear per-language ergonomic examples and tests. The library must be incremental (can validate partial payloads), composable with existing SDK call layers, and instrumentable (hooks for telemetry/tracing).
design:
Key design choices:
- Default permissive validator: accept unknown extra keys and coerce simple type mismatches. Provide 'strict' option to enforce exact schema.
- Policy-first coercion: a pluggable policy object (coerce_numbers, coerce_enums, default_fill) that can be shared across SDKs.
- Streaming validator: keep a lightweight incremental JSON token walker that can validate present fields as they arrive and emit a 'partial_valid' signal; when final chunk arrives, run full validation.
- Retry & idempotency: invocation helpers attach an idempotency token header and persist last-n KB of request pre-state for safe retries; allow user-supplied 'is_idempotent' callback for custom tooling.
- Backoff policy: jittered exponential with configurable max attempts and per-attempt timeout. Failures are categorized: transient (retryable), terminal (fail immediately), and resumable (for streaming).
- API ergonomics: keep helpers small surface: validate_schema(), coerce_and_validate(), StreamReassembler, invoke_with_retry().
- Interop: define canonical JSON schema fingerprint (sha256 of canonicalized schema) to allow serverside quick-compat checks.
tasks: Draft permissive validator core: coerce numbers, basic enum fuzzy-matching, default fill behavior
Implement incremental JSON token walker for streaming partial validation
Design and implement language-agnostic coercion policy spec and fingerprinting
Expose ergonomics in Python, TS, Go clients with idiomatic APIs
Add idempotency token plumbing and retry wrapper with categorized failures
Integrate telemetry hooks (events for partial_valid, final_valid, retry_attempt)
Write unit + property tests covering coercion edge cases and streaming reassembly
Create docs/examples and add to SDK quickstarts
Security review for idempotency persistence and potential PII in logs
acceptance_criteria: Validator accepts model outputs with extra unknown keys by default and coerces simple mismatches when policy enables it
Strict mode rejects unknown fields and mismatched types and is opt-in
Streaming reassembler can validate partial payloads and recover after a lost connection (resume semantics documented)
invoke_with_retry attaches idempotency key and respects max_attempts/backoff policy; retries only categorized transient errors
Language examples exist (Python/TS/Go) and pass their respective CI suites
Telemetry hooks emit partial_valid, final_valid, retry_attempt events and are documented
No sensitive payload is logged by default; security review sign-off obtained
